messages.content:
Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
The collisions are elastic reflections in which each ant reverses its own velocity (preserving its speed). Because the ants have unequal speeds, these reflections are not equivalent to the ants exchanging velocities or passing through one another; the motion must be simulated event by event.

- At \(t=0\):  
  \(A\) at \(10\) with velocity \(+3\),  
  \(B\) at \(40\) with velocity \(-1\),  
  \(C\) at \(80\) with velocity \(-2\).

- \(A\) and \(B\) approach each other at relative speed \(4\). They collide after  
  \[
  t_1=\frac{30}{4}=\frac{15}{2}.
  \]
  The collision point is \(32.5\). Velocities become  
  \(A:-3\), \(B:+1\).  
  In the same interval \(C\) reaches \(65\) (still velocity \(-2\)).

- \(B\) (now \(+1\)) and \(C\) (velocity \(-2\)) approach each other at relative speed \(3\). The distance is \(32.5\), so they collide after  
  \[
  t_2=\frac{65/2}{3}=\frac{65}{6}.
  \]
  Simultaneously \(A\), traveling left at speed \(3\) from \(32.5\), reaches the left end and falls off.  
  The \(B\)-\(C\) collision occurs at position \(130/3\). Velocities become  
  \(B:-1\), \(C:+2\).

- The two remaining ants now move away from each other:  
  - \(B\) travels left distance \(130/3\) at speed \(1\), requiring time \(130/3\);  
  - \(C\) travels right distance \(170/3\) at speed \(2\), requiring time \(85/3\).

Adding the successive intervals gives the fall-off times  
\[
\frac{15}{2}+\frac{65}{6}+\frac{130}{3}=\frac{185}{3}
\]  
for \(B\) and  
\[
\frac{15}{2}+\frac{65}{6}+\frac{85}{3}=\frac{140}{3}
\]  
for \(C\). The later of these instants is \(185/3\).

No further collisions are possible after the second reflection, so the last ant leaves the rod at exactly \(185/3\) seconds.

ANSWER: 185/3
